html:
On 16 September 1963 Malaya joined with Singapore, Sabah (North Borneo) and Sarawak to form Malaysia. The idea had been put forward by Tunku Abdul Rahman in 1961.

Adding the Borneo states balanced Singapore's large Chinese population. Brunei stayed out after the Brunei revolt, and Indonesia and the Philippines opposed the federation; Indonesia answered with the Konfrontasi.

Singapore left in 1965 (see Singapore leaves Malaysia). Sabah and Sarawak kept special powers over immigration and land, and the date is now Malaysia Day. See also Sarawak.
